Diagnosis.submission:
Root cause: rate never reaches serving: each pod reads config, logs the correct datastore URL mongodb-rate:27017, then panics ~12s later in database initialization with an unreachable-servers error, looping continuously [tr_88a01606ee27]. The dial deadline expiring at connect time, with no query-timeout or pool entries, points at mongodb-rate being present-but-unserving rather than at anything wrong inside rate. Config correctness, request-path bugs, and pool exhaustion in rate are each excluded by rate's own log [tr_88a01606ee27]. mongodb-rate's log query was rejected by Loki with a 400 on a malformed pod regex, so the culprit's own voice was never heard [tr_46428f62c4a4]; both metric baselines failed for structural instrumentation reasons [tr_bfcbc09c5459, tr_f6ed97dbcbce] and all change-history queries died on a parse error [tr_4d406f3b84ac, tr_1c9653913a48, tr_c183cd3a076b]. The surviving mechanism consistent with the one good signal is that mongodb-rate's process is stopped while its socket still exists, so rate hangs to its connect deadline and dies.
Faulty component: mongodb-rate
Fault type: process_freeze
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- The rate pod repeatedly starts, reads config and the datastore URL (mongodb-rate:27017), then panics during database initialization with an unreachable-servers error roughly 12 seconds after each start — a tight crash-restart loop with cycles beginning around 04:36:51 and 04:37:58. (found, from logql_query on rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The panic originates in the service's own startup path (database initialization called from main), so the process never reaches the point of serving traffic; no request-handling or gRPC-serving log lines appear in the window. (found, from logql_query on rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The failure mode is connection establishment to the rate datastore, not query slowness: there are no query-timeout or slow-operation entries, only the immediate unreachable-server panic at connect time. (found, from logql_query on rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- rate is up but degraded, returning errors or timing out on individual requests under load (ruled_out, from logql_query on rate; why: The process panics during startup before serving; there are no request-level logs at all, so it is not a partial degradation of a running service.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Misconfiguration in rate — missing or malformed datastore URL, bad config, or TLS handshake failure (ruled_out, from logql_query on rate; why: Config is read successfully, the expected datastore endpoint is logged on every attempt, and TLS is reported disabled; the failure happens after config load, at connect.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A bug in rate's request-handling or business logic caused the crash (ruled_out, from logql_query on rate; why: The stack trace points to the database initialization call from main, not to any handler path.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Datastore connection pool exhaustion or query timeouts from sustained traffic (ruled_out, from logql_query on rate; why: No timeout or pool-related entries appear; the single repeated failure is inability to reach any server at initial connect.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A one-off transient blip that has already self-resolved (ruled_out, from logql_query on rate; why: At least two full start-and-panic cycles occur back to back through the end of the window, showing a persistent crash loop.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The log query never executed: Loki returned HTTP 400 Bad Request, so the result is an error rather than an empty result set. No log data for mongodb-rate was retrieved for the requested window. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The failure is client-side query construction, not a backend outage — the request reached the Loki endpoint and was rejected as malformed, consistent with the escaped-hyphen pod regex alternation in the selector being invalid. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The question of whether mongodb-rate was starting, crash-looping, refusing connections, or absent at 04:36:49 remains entirely unanswered by this result. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- mongodb-rate emitted no logs in the window, implying the process was absent or never started (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; why: The empty payload is an error artifact, not a successful zero-row response. A query that returned 400 cannot be read as evidence of log absence, so 'silent pod' cannot be inferred here.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Loki is down or the log pipeline is broken, which is why nothing came back (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; why: Loki answered the HTTP request with a 400 status, meaning the service was reachable and processing requests; the rejection was of the query itself.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The time window was wrong or outside retention, causing the gap (ruled_out, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; why: The request was rejected before range evaluation on a bad-request basis; the start/end parameters were accepted into the URL and are not implicated in the error.; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb\-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The error-ratio metric query for the rate service returned no data at all; the backing Prometheus holds no span-derived metrics for this service, so the result is an availability gap rather than a measurement of zero errors. (found, from metric_baseline on rate)
- No error rate, latency percentile, request volume, or connection/saturation figures for rate are observable in this window or in the preceding baseline window from this source. (found, from metric_baseline on rate)
- The absence of a reported error ratio for rate means the service was healthy and erroring at zero through 04:36:49. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on rate; why: The query explicitly failed rather than returning a zero series, so no health conclusion can be drawn from the empty result.)
- Span-metric-based dashboards or alerts for rate could have fired or stayed silent meaningfully during the incident, making their state a useful signal. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on rate; why: The service emits nothing that becomes span metrics in this Prometheus, so any such alert path is inert for rate and its silence carries no information.)
- This metrics path can be used to confirm or exclude rate as the origin of the 04:36:49 event. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on rate; why: The data source is structurally empty for this service, so it can neither implicate nor exonerate rate; the question must be answered from traces, logs, or infrastructure-level metrics instead.)
- The error-ratio metric query for mongodb-rate returned no data and reported a query failure: the metric is derived from span-based telemetry that this environment's Prometheus does not hold for this service, so connection counts, memory/cache usage, operation latency, and error counters could not be retrieved for either the incident window or the preceding baseline window. (found, from metric_baseline on mongodb-rate)
- The absence is an instrumentation gap, not an observation of healthy or zero error traffic — mongodb-rate emits no traces that would be converted into these metrics, so the metric series does not exist at all. (found, from metric_baseline on mongodb-rate)
- mongodb-rate's error rate is flat/zero across the onset, so the database can be cleared as a contributor (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on mongodb-rate; why: The query did not return a zero series; it failed because the underlying metric is unavailable for this service. No inference about mongodb-rate's error behaviour — healthy or unhealthy — can be drawn from this result.)
- Prometheus metrics are the right avenue for characterising mongodb-rate connection saturation, cache pressure, or operation latency in this incident (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on mongodb-rate; why: The metric backend holds no span-derived series for mongodb-rate across the full window and baseline, so repeating metric queries of this family will not yield data. Investigation must shift to direct database telemetry, server logs, or the latency observed by mongodb-rate's callers.)
- The empty result indicates mongodb-rate was down or scraped-but-silent during the incident window (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on mongodb-rate; why: The result carries an explicit query-failure reason tied to missing metric definitions, and the baseline window before the onset is equally empty. A service that went down during onset would show data in the baseline window; uniform absence points to the metric never existing.)
- The change-history query for the rate service over the requested window did not return data; it terminated with a parsing error, so no change records were retrieved. (found, from change_history on rate)
- The failure appears to be a malformed/truncated response payload from the change-log source rather than a filter returning zero matches, so the change surface for rate in this window remains entirely unobserved. (found, from change_history on rate)
- The change-log has been checked and rate had no deployments, config edits, or pool/database-setting changes in the window. (ruled_out, from change_history on rate; why: The result is an error, not an empty set. Absence of returned records here carries no evidential weight about whether changes occurred, and this hypothesis must not be treated as confirmed.)
- A change-driven cause can be excluded and investigation should move on to load, dependency, or infrastructure explanations. (ruled_out, from change_history on rate; why: Excluding change requires evidence of no change. This query produced none, so the change hypothesis stays fully open and the query should be retried, ideally with a narrower window or smaller page size to avoid the truncated payload.)

Reasoning:
Only one dispatch returned real data. It shows rate crash-looping in startup DB init against the correct endpoint, which localizes the fault to mongodb-rate rather than rate. The deadline-shaped failure (uniform ~12s to panic, no partial success, no slow-query lines) fits a datastore that does not complete the handshake. Distinguishing freeze from partition or a dead pod requires mongodb-rate's log, which was never retrieved because the selector was malformed; that gap is why confidence is low and why the class is a best-fit, not a settled finding. The mongodb-* and reservation alerts are consistent with the same blast radius propagating to callers.

Alternatives considered:
1. mongodb-rate: mongodb-rate is running but network-isolated from the hotel-reservation namespace, so rate's connects time out. (network_partition). Ranked lower because: Indistinguishable from a freeze using rate's log alone; demoted only because nothing yet shows mongodb-rate alive and complaining. The unread mongodb-rate log would decide it.
2. mongodb-rate: A change to mongodb-rate (image, port, auth, or storage setting) left it unable to start or listening wrongly, and rate cannot connect as a result. (bad_deploy). Ranked lower because: No change record was ever retrieved — every change query errored — so this rests on no evidence at all, whereas the connect-deadline shape is directly observed.

Open questions:
- mongodb-rate's own logs were never read (Loki 400) — re-run with a corrected pod selector to see whether mongod is silent (freeze), complaining it cannot reach anything (partition), refusing with no space left (disk fill), or absent entirely.
- Pod/container state for mongodb-rate: is it Running, CrashLoopBackOff, Pending, or evicted? No infrastructure-level check was performed.
- All change-history queries failed on a parse error, so a deploy, image, or config change to mongodb-rate or rate in the preceding 24h remains entirely unobserved; the window queried also started at onset rather than before it.
- Whether the other alerting mongodb-* services share the same failure, which would point to a node- or cluster-level cause rather than one datastore.
